Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti

Subtropical Samegrelo with its canyons and Upper Svaneti with its towers — one region, two entirely different worlds.

Click a marker for details. Coloured lines are ready-made road trips.

This administrative region joins two quite different countries. Below lies Samegrelo: warm, humid and flat, planted with tea and citrus, centred on Zugdidi and the Dadiani Palace museum, a European-style residence with a botanical garden and a collection connected to the Bonaparte family. Martvili Canyon on the Abasha river is visited by boat between limestone walls, and Nokalakevi, the Archaeopolis of Byzantine sources, preserves late antique walls and a tunnel running down to the river.

Northwards the road begins to climb at the Enguri Dam, an arch dam with the long turquoise Jvari Reservoir behind it, and within three hours it delivers you into a different climate altogether. Upper Svaneti is a high mountain province with its own language, polyphony and architecture. Mestia holds the Svaneti Museum, rich in icons and manuscripts, among stone defensive towers; above it are the Hatsvali and Tetnuldi ski areas, and a forest path leads to the Chalaadi Glacier. Ushguli, a group of four villages at 2,100 metres beneath Mount Shkhara, is UNESCO-listed. The Koruldi Lakes are reached only on foot or by jeep.

Seasonality is double. Samegrelo is accessible all year, while Svaneti is at its best from June to September, with a separate winter season for skiing. Three to four days is the minimum that makes sense, and most travellers give it more.

Best for

  • A four-day run: Zugdidi, Mestia and Ushguli
  • Svan towers and high mountain scenery in summer
  • Martvili Canyon and Nokalakevi in a single day
  • Winter skiing at Hatsvali and Tetnuldi

Driving conditions

The first thing to accept is distance: Mestia is around 470 km from Tbilisi and eight to nine hours of driving. Doing it as a return trip in one day is not realistic, so plan a night in Zugdidi, Kutaisi or Mestia itself.

The road from Zugdidi to Mestia is asphalt and technically sound, but 130 km takes roughly three hours: continuous bends, narrow sections in the Enguri gorge, rockfall zones and livestock on the carriageway. After rain or snowmelt, stones on the road are routine rather than exceptional. In winter the road to Mestia normally stays open, but winter tyres are required and chains are worth having.

Above Mestia everything changes. The final stretch to Ushguli is gravel and needs a high-clearance vehicle; the track to the Koruldi Lakes is 4x4 only. Taking a low car onto either is not covered by rental insurance. Fuel is available in Zugdidi and Mestia and effectively nowhere in between, so fill up before the climb.

In this region — 9 places

Town

Mestia and the Svan Towers

Upper Svaneti's main town at 1,500 m — medieval stone defence towers, two strong museums and the trailhead for every route in the region.

  • Time needed: 4 h
  • From Tbilisi: 470 km · 8:30
  • Car needed: Crossover / SUV
Town

Ushguli

One of Europe's highest permanently inhabited settlements at 2,100 m, under Mount Shkhara — UNESCO-listed as part of Upper Svaneti.

  • Time needed: 4 h
  • From Tbilisi: 515 km · 10:30
  • Car needed: Off-road 4x4
Mountain

Chalaadi Glacier

The most accessible glacier near Mestia — a short drive up the valley and a two-hour walk to the ice tongue.

  • Time needed: 4 h
  • From Tbilisi: 480 km · 8:50
  • Car needed: Crossover / SUV
Lake

Koruldi Lakes

Small alpine pools at 2,740 m above Mestia, facing Mount Ushba — reachable only by 4x4 or on foot.

  • Time needed: 3 h
  • From Tbilisi: 480 km · 9:30
  • Car needed: Off-road 4x4
Ski area

Hatsvali and Tetnuldi Ski Areas

Mestia's two ski zones — Hatsvali with sheltered forest runs, and Tetnuldi, where the lifts pass 3,000 metres.

  • Time needed: 6 h
  • From Tbilisi: 478 km · 8:50
  • Car needed: Crossover / SUV
Canyon

Martvili Canyon

A turquoise river between limestone walls, with boardwalks and a short boat ride — Samegrelo's most visited natural site.

  • Time needed: 2 h
  • From Tbilisi: 310 km · 4:30
  • Car needed: Economy class
Lake

Enguri Dam and Jvari Reservoir

A 271-metre arch dam on the road to Mestia, with a long turquoise reservoir stretching behind it.

  • Time needed: 1 h
  • From Tbilisi: 350 km · 5:10
  • Car needed: Economy class
Museum

Dadiani Palace, Zugdidi

The residence of the princes of Mingrelia set in a botanical garden — Napoleon's death mask and the family collection.

  • Time needed: 2 h
  • From Tbilisi: 320 km · 4:40
  • Car needed: Economy class
Archaeology

Nokalakevi (Archaeopolis)

A fortified city from the Lazic Wars above the Tekhuri river — walls, a secret tunnel and an active excavation.

  • Time needed: 2 h
  • From Tbilisi: 300 km · 4:30
  • Car needed: Economy class
